# C array initializer conformance

These 69 isolated C projects contain 14,678 canonical lines, including AST separators (14,332 nonempty records) generated by Joern v4.0.555. Each project is imported and closed independently, so a shared TYPE registry cannot conceal extra types. `expected.txt` contains every AST, NODES, EDGES and FLOWS record emitted by `isolated-oracle.sc`, with only the `AST|` transport prefix removed. The script is the shared oracle inside a sorted per-directory import loop. No expected graph facts are edited or filtered to obtain equality. The shared projection selects properties and edge kinds; it is not a comparison of every Joern property, and its existing newline escaping is not injective.

The sources cover local/global sized and unsized arrays; brace, string, concatenated-string and wide-string initializers; nested and flat multidimensional arrays; unsigned, floating, const and pointer elements; compound literals; scalar brace initializers; indexed and nested indexed designators; GNU range designators and empty brace initializers; mixed declarations and `for` initializers. Additional cases preserve callback-array behavior and distinguish object types from parameter types. `char *value[2]` has object type `char*[2]`, while the pinned parameter spelling is `char[2]*`. Object pointer-to-array spelling and nested declarator quirks are retained as observed, not inferred from a blanket type normalizer.

The pinned lowering emits all LOCALs, then all local array allocations, then all explicit initializers for a declaration. A sized local string array therefore has both allocation and initialization assignments. An unsized leading dimension does not allocate. Global arrays with an explicit initializer omit the separate dimension expression; a global unsized declaration without one retains an empty arrayInitializer. Brace lists become recursive arrayInitializer CALLs. Indexed designators are assignment children of synthetic BLOCKs.

The production tests compare complete graphs and check allocation ordering and source locations separately. Parsed direct declarator spans let allocation and initialization views overlap without moving a following statement or borrowing a nested declaration. Source line assertions include preexisting string literals, mixed scalar/array declarations, duplicate method text, an array-size call followed by the same call, and separate lexical blocks. `array_flows/outcomes.txt` retains five results from a fresh live `reachableBy` query: two positive and three negative. The compound-literal negative is the pinned oracle's outcome; it is not a general array alias-analysis guarantee.

Three full nonconformant diagnostics remain under `diagnostics/`: struct field designators, combined field/subscript designators, and member array/pointer type spelling. Each retains source, full live graph, accepted-baseline output, candidate output and complete difference. Field-designator lowering and broader member/tagged-type handling are outside this primitive-array family. Existing repository diagnostics remain intact.

Replay the isolated oracle from a fresh working directory with JDK 21 and the pinned runtime:

```sh
JAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk21 PATH=/path/to/jdk21/bin:$PATH \
  /path/to/joern-cli/joern --script /absolute/path/to/isolated-oracle.sc \
  --param inputPath=/absolute/path/to/array-initializers/cases
```

Run the production tests from the Rust workspace, using a build target dedicated to the current checkout:

```sh
cargo test -p joern-parity --test array_initializers
cargo test -p cpg-analysis --test canonical_c_array_initializers
```

At the array-only commit, 61 of these 69 graphs are exact (accepted baseline: 8). Eight cases remain different only in reaching-definition facts. `pre-rd-diagnostics/` retains their complete array-only graphs and differences against the corresponding `cases/<name>/expected.txt`. The full-graph test stays enabled and fails until the separately owned reaching-definition repair is integrated. All other 386 workspace tests pass; none are ignored or filtered. The existing 308 comparison blocks remain required.

`measurement.json` binds source snapshots, binaries, fresh oracle output, fixtures, complete comparisons and validation commands. Timings are measured execution times for those runs, not a port-completeness percentage.

The integrated fourth batch also includes the independently reviewed operator-argument mapping and missing-CODE reaching-definition repairs. All 69 complete graphs now pass; the eight array-only differences remain preserved as historical evidence. See the fourth-batch acceptance receipt for final combined-source validation.
